binance.name: Binance
on: Enable Spot & Margin Trading (only if the bot trades spot)
Enable Futures (only if the bot trades futures)
off: Any transfer permission the bot doesn't need
notes: Binance: a system-generated (HMAC) key with unrestricted IP access can only have the Reading permission.
Binance: IP access restriction is mandatory before Withdrawals can be enabled. A trading bot shouldn't need Withdrawals at all.

bybit.name: Bybit
on: Read-Write (only if the bot places orders; Read-Only for dashboards and tax tools)
Spot Trade and/or Contract Trade (Orders, Positions), only what the strategy uses
off: Wallet: Account Transfer / Subaccount Transfer unless the bot truly needs it
notes: Bybit API docs: a key with no IP bound becomes invalid after 90 days; binding an IP removes that expiry.
Bybit: API keys can only be created on the website, not in the app.

bitget.name: Bitget
on: Trade (only the product types the bot uses)
notes: Bitget: you set a passphrase when you create the key; it can't be recovered or changed. If you lose it, delete the key and make a new one.
Bitget strongly recommends binding an IP address; withdrawals are only possible from a whitelisted IP.

okx.name: OKX
on: Trade (only if the bot places orders)
notes: OKX: each key can bind up to 20 IP addresses.
OKX: keys not bound to an IP that have Trade or Withdraw permission are deleted after 14 days of inactivity.

coinzoom.name: CoinZoom
on: Trading access for the one service you chose
off: Sharing the key with anyone else
Your password or 2FA codes (CoinZoom: never share them)
notes: CoinZoom: create keys at trade.coinzoom.com, Settings, API Trading, Generate Key. You choose how many days the key stays active (up to 365). Web only, not the app.
CoinZoom: enable Whitelist IP addresses when creating a key, and remove the key in the same screen to cut a service off. Removing a key does not cancel any subscription with the service.

waves.label: Wave 2
waves.when: 1 to 2 weeks after December 1 (announced as a range, no exact date)

binance.-2015: Invalid API-key, IP, or permissions for action: wrong key/environment, IP not trusted, or missing permission (unrestricted HMAC keys can only read).

bybit.10003: API key is invalid: key and domain don't match (mainnet, testnet, mainnet-demo, testnet-demo) or key expired (no IP bound: 90 days).

redflags: Promises or implies a fixed or guaranteed return.
Pays for recruiting, or ranks members by downline deposits.
Asks for withdrawal permission, your password, or 2FA codes.
Asks you to send funds to its wallet instead of keeping them on your own exchange account.
Regulators have issued warnings about the operator or the people behind it.
Pressure to hurry: limited spots, countdowns, deposit more to get in earlier.
No named company, address or licence you can check.
Performance shown only as screenshots or promo videos, no verifiable track record.
checklist: Only the permissions the bot needs (read + trade).
Key bound to the bot IP addresses if it publishes them.
A separate key for this one bot.
You know where to delete the key.
Expiry set if the exchange offers one.
Secret and passphrase stored in a password manager, never in chats or screenshots.
Exchange app installed only from an official store or site, not an APK link.
Operator checked on your regulator register.
